chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

He was asked about a man who performed the obligatory Tawaf, but did not pray the two Rak'ahs; then he performed the Tawaf between al-Safa and al-Marwa; and after that he performed the Tawaf of the Women (Tawaf al-Nisa'), and did not pray for that Tawaf either, until he remembered at al-Abtah. He said: 'He should return to the Maqam Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and pray.'

key_terms.الْأَبْطَحِ: The flat open area between Mecca and Medina, often used as a place of remembrance or prayer
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf of the Women (the fourth circumambulation)
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The obligatory circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The Station of Abraham, a specific location in the Masjid al-Haram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to pray the two Rak'ahs after Tawaf and Sa'i?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, the Imam clarifies that neglecting the two Rak'ahs of prayer after Tawaf al-Farid and Sa'i does not invalidate the Tawaf itself, but requires the pilgrim to return specifically to the Maqam Ibrahim to perform the missed prayers. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the distinct legal status of the prayer following Tawaf as a confirmed Sunnah (Sunnat al-Tawaf) rather than an integral pillar, ensuring the ritual's completeness through rectification at its designated spot.
